title: Marvel vs. Capcom Fighting Collection Is a Love Letter to the Arcade
excerpt: Capcom's seven-game compilation isn't just nostalgia bait — it's the most accessible these classics have ever been, and a reminder of why crossover fighters mattered.

children.text: There's a specific sound a CRT made when X-Men vs. Street Fighter booted up in a crowded arcade. The Fighting Collection can't give you the sticky floor or the smell of the food court, but it gets remarkably close to everything that mattered.

Rollback netcode is the headline feature, and it delivers. Matches feel crisp in a way these games never did online before. For a generation that only knew these titles through emulation, that alone justifies the price of entry.

title: Why Representation in Games Still Matters in 2026
excerpt: The industry loves to talk about how far it's come. The numbers, and the people behind them, tell a more complicated story.

children.text: Every year a studio puts out a sizzle reel about inclusion. Every year the credits still look mostly the same. Progress is real, but it is uneven, and pretending otherwise does a disservice to the people fighting for a seat at the table.

title: Fresno's Indie Game Scene Is Quietly Thriving
excerpt: Away from the coastal studios, a small but stubborn community of Central Valley developers is building something of their own.

children.text: You won't find a triple-A campus in Fresno. What you will find is a Discord server with a few hundred developers, a monthly meetup at a downtown coffee shop, and a surprising number of shipped games with Central Valley fingerprints all over them.
